question: Can an immutable repository identity read immediately before and after a name-addressed staged write make same-name delete/recreate safe when the stage is explicitly non-authoritative until the postcheck?

observations.current_chat_repo_identity_read: The current GitHub connector get_repo call returned repository numeric id 1325150959 for bachikoljunior-blip/note. The current generic approved GitHub REST fetch of GET /repos/bachikoljunior-blip/note returned both id 1325150959 and node_id R_kgDOTvwy7w.
observations.current_chat_write_addressing: The currently inspected contents create/update primitives address the repository by repository_full_name and path; they do not accept repository numeric/node identity as an atomic write precondition. Part135 previously established the same name-addressing limitation for the inspected Git object/ref composition.
observations.public_get_repository: GitHub's official REST 'Get a repository' documentation shows repository responses containing both id and node_id while the request path is owner/repo.
observations.public_global_node_id: GitHub's official global-node-ID guide states that REST node_id corresponds to the GraphQL Node id and supports direct node lookup. GitHub's global-ID migration guide says the new IDs are unique and can be relied on directly as references.
observations.identity_lifetime_scope_guard: The inspected public sources support uniqueness/direct-reference use of global node IDs but do not explicitly state a temporal never-reuse guarantee for a deleted repository's node_id followed by same-name recreation. This model therefore treats non-rebinding across delete/recreate as a conservative assumption, not a proven provider guarantee.

finite_model.retry_rule: Every later retry restarts from the repository-identity precheck; no same-run wait/backoff occurs. A stable stage/effect ID from the prior fixed-incarnation slices is assumed for same-incarnation staging dedupe.
finite_model.identity_rule: Precheck must equal frozen repository identity I0. Postcheck must also equal I0. Identity mismatch or unavailable postcheck prevents publication. The model assumes a recreated repository has a different identity; provider-guaranteed temporal non-rebinding remains outside proven scope.

stage_is_authoritative_then_postcheck.unsafe_slice: all 8 between_precheck_and_stage traces, independent of copied history and transport

nonauthoritative_stage_postcheck_then_na.unsafe_slice: all 8 after_postcheck_before_publication traces; the postcheck succeeded for I0, recreation then occurs, and the later name-addressed publication resolves to I1

assumptions: staging has no externally authoritative side effect
all authoritative publication is deferred until the final gate
the final publication gate atomically verifies the current repository identity equals frozen I0 while applying the effect
repository identity is not rebound to a distinct recreated object

new_narrowing.precheck_value: A repository identity precheck does prevent writes when recreation happened before the attempt begins and forces later retries after response loss/rate-limit interruption to re-evaluate incarnation instead of blindly resuming a stale name-bound effect.
new_narrowing.postcheck_value: When staging is truly non-authoritative, a postcheck converts recreation during the staged write window into fail-closed containment. In the 8 between_precheck_and_stage traces, a wrong-incarnation stage can occur, but publication is suppressed when the postcheck observes I1 rather than I0.
new_narrowing.detection_not_prevention: If the staged write itself is authoritative, the same 8 between-precheck-and-stage traces are already unsafe before the postcheck. A later mismatch only detects the error and cannot retract the authoritative effect.
new_narrowing.remaining_window: If publication after a successful postcheck is still name-addressed, recreation after postcheck but before publication creates 8/40 wrong-incarnation authoritative effects. Therefore the sandwich narrows but does not eliminate the incarnation problem; it moves the required atomic identity check to the final publication boundary.
new_narrowing.copied_history_result: Copied same-history/state does not defeat the sandwich when repository identity changes, because the decision compares identity rather than history/blob equality. It becomes unsafe again only if the provider can rebind/reuse the same identity for the recreated repository or if publication omits the identity fence.
new_narrowing.transport_result: Response loss, rate-limit interruption and postcheck failure remain fail-closed for authoritative publication when every later invocation restarts at precheck and publication requires a successful current postcheck. They may leave orphan/non-authoritative staging writes; cleanup is a separate liveness/storage concern, not an authoritative-effect pass.

minimal_unresolved_children: No inspected current Chat write primitive atomically binds the final authoritative publication to the frozen repository numeric/node identity; all inspected repository writes are name-addressed.
The identity sandwich is safe only when staging is non-authoritative. If repository write visibility is itself the authoritative external effect, the postcheck is detection-only.

Provider-guaranteed temporal non-rebinding/non-reuse of a deleted repository global node ID across same-name recreation is not explicit in the inspected public documentation and remains a conservative assumption boundary.
scope_guard: This is a bounded 120-scenario synthetic model plus current Chat connector-schema/response inspection and cited public GitHub documentation. It does not mutate or recreate repositories, does not prove actual GitHub ID reuse behavior, does not cover arbitrary external sinks, Byzantine actors, authorization-token rollback, or publication systems that offer their own incarnation fencing.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.richer_mode_protected_manual_execution_d: none for this bounded modeling/documentation slice
zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.rate_limit_behavior: rate-limit interruption checkpoints to a later invocation and restarts from identity precheck; no same-run retry/wait/backoff is required

exact_continuation: Part137: execute one bounded immutable-object-as-authority leaf. Hold Parts128-136 fixed. Test whether the final authoritative effect can be redesigned so no second name-addressed publication is needed: stage one immutable Git object/commit under frozen repository identity, publish only an immutable object handle plus repository node identity, and require every consumer/retry to re-resolve that identity before use. Enumerate same-name recreation before and after handle creation, copied Git object/history, object absence in replacement, response loss, rate-limit interruption/later retry, stale-handle replay and consumer-side name fallback. Treat any consumer that must resolve by owner/repo without identity fencing, any unavailable direct node/object read, or any external publication step as an unresolved child. Persist exact tested scope, zero-cost/zero-quota assessment, unresolved child and nonempty continuation; do not execute another leaf in the same invocation.
